acceptedChanges: Append-only stream retains completed blocks only after a full blank line outside a fence. Reuses unchanged safe parser for the unfinished tail on every existing RAF; no delayed rendering.

Original renderMessage implementation remains byte-for-byte unchanged. Complete stable portion and unfinished tail concatenate to the same DOM because a blank line outside a fence flushes paragraph/list state and inline tokens cannot cross a newline.
Panel passes only text since the last RAF to one renderer owned by the active run. Existing at-bottom decision and RAF scheduling are unchanged.

Every finish path disposes renderer text/node/container references, clears its owner field, and performs the existing full final render. New Chat invokes stop before clearing messages. Queued RAF behavior across finalization and a new run tested.
No provider history, retention, permission, URL interpretation, reduced-motion code, retry logic or sync code changed.

rejectedIdeas: No cadence reduction, debounce, deferred full-reply rendering or hidden streaming text.
No history caps, virtualization, provider history changes or dropping user data.
Did not commit individual lines, headings, list items or incomplete fences: conservative blank-line boundary keeps exact parser state simple.
Avoided extra DOM wrapper or per-frame DocumentFragment allocations; forwarding target removes only mutable top-level nodes.
objections: Long single paragraphs, uninterrupted lists, and open code fences have no stable blank boundary, so retain full-tail quadratic rendering work. Added scanner does one extra pass over completed lines. No speed improvement is claimed for these cases; actual latency remains unmeasured.

Counters measure explicit renderer input and synthetic DOM allocations, not all JS allocations, substring representation, regex work, DOM garbage collection, real memory, CPU, energy or browser speed.
Tail rebuilding can still replace focused/selected nodes in the unfinished tail, as the old renderer did for the full reply. Stable prefix nodes now retain identity.
Fake DOM validates tree structure, link properties, node identity and explicit scrollTop decisions, not browser automatic scroll anchoring/layout or assistive announcements.
